slices.name: ws01-24-semantic-colours-status-raw
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 24 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD 4e4ad3a (slice 23); the base for diffs is 4e4ad3a. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (Ordering rules, the acceptance table and its T1 row (line 57), Decisions (Tokens from step 21, and Ink and grounds, The brand navy and Colour classes move by script and reviewed map from step 23, lines 680 to 682), Deviations (step 23), Verify items (step 23), Follow-ups (Dark mode on pages not converted yet (step 21), and from step 23: K reviews the step 23 judgement calls, Navy borders and rings, Navy tints in dark mode, Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS, Light islands that stay light in dark mode, Quoted strings in comment prose, lines 1143 to 1154), and steps 21 to 23), docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md section 1 (the decided look) and section WS01 (the base and dark palettes, 'StatusBadge always renders a text label. Its tones map to status tokens' at line 303, which is order 26, and the gold text clean-up, which is order 25), src/index.css (both @theme blocks at lines 34 to 121, with the status utilities at lines 66 to 81; the legacy :root semantic and status tokens at lines 157 to 197; the new-look base, dark, live, scholastic and heritage blocks at lines 249, 287, 322, 365 and 412; the shadcn re-pointing at lines 440 to 471 and the focus ring rules at lines 473 to 507), node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css (the emerald, red, amber, yellow, green, blue, purple, slate and gray scales), scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.ts and scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.map.json (this slice runs the same script with a second map through --map), test/unit/semantic-map.test.ts, semantic-map-cascade.test.ts, semantic-map-grounds.test.ts, semantic-colours-edges.test.ts, redesign-status-step23.test.ts, tokens.test.ts, token-utilities.test.ts, contrast.test.ts and the helpers test/unit/helpers/cssTokens.ts and jsxClasses.ts (how index.css is parsed, how a utility is compiled with Tailwind's own compile(), and how class strings and their grounds are read with the TypeScript parser), src/components/StatusBadge.tsx, and the browser test harness (playwright.config.ts, test/a11y/support.ts, baseline.ts, baseline.json, dark-spot.spec.ts, dark-grounds.spec.ts, smoke.spec.ts, tokens.spec.ts, known-violations.json) so the flag-off baseline comparison stays green and the dark spot run is narrowed to what is still owned later. The manifest entries for orders 25 and 26 say what this slice leaves to them (25: text-lca-gold, StatusBadge's text-[#7a5c00] and PageHero's text-[#f0d07a], and the gold guard test; 26: StatusBadge's status prop mapped to status tokens, with the tone and on props unchanged for current callers). The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ: <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 24) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. node_modules is installed; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy.

Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. Dependencies are exact-pinned (no caret) at versions at least two weeks old, with package-lock.json updated by npm install. The branch tip is 4e4ad3a (slice 23), the same commit origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carries in this container, and the working tree is clean; the local main ref in this container is 4c1a466 and does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against 4e4ad3a.

Build exactly this. Part two of the theme-ability pass: status colours and raw hex. The same codemod gets a second map. Emerald and red status text and fills become the status tokens (ok, bad, or the matching status-* utility). Gray and slate stragglers become ink-muted or border-hairline. The remaining arbitrary hex text and background classes (text-[#...] 39, bg-[#...] 8) become tokens, except StatusBadge's light gold text-[#7a5c00] and PageHero's text-[#f0d07a], which slice 25 handles with the gold work. Each mapping again resolves under the legacy :root to the colour it replaces, and semantic-map.test.ts is extended to cover it. Add a ratchet, test/unit/raw-colours.test.ts. It fails when text-lca-navy, bg-white, raw emerald or red status classes, or arbitrary hex colour classes appear in TSX outside the allowlist fixture test/unit/fixtures/raw-colours-allowlist.json, which holds club colour swatches and user-chosen club colours with a reason per line. A person reviews tinted banners and badges, and the judgement calls go in REDESIGN_STATUS.md.

Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): Legitimate raw colours: AdminClubPage.tsx:391 uses '#c8a94a' as placeholder text in a colour input (not a colour class); AdminPage.tsx:531 uses it as a background fallback for a club swatch; club colours come from clubColors.ts and are user data. (re-checked at 4e4ad3a: the lines have moved to AdminClubPage.tsx line 395, placeholder="#c8a94a" on the colour input, and AdminPage.tsx line 532, style={{ backgroundColor: club.color || '#c8a94a' }}; clubColors.ts is now src/areas/clubs/clubColors.ts, moved in step 17. Neither is a class, so a class scan never sees them: club colours are inline styles throughout, and the TSX files hold 17 quoted hex literals in 9 files, all inline styles or data (LCAMap.tsx 5, AdminEmailPage.tsx 4, and one each in WorkspacePage, TournamentsPage, ClubDetailPage, AdminPage, AdminClubPage, AgendaList and ClubLocationPicker).) Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at 4e4ad3a with ripgrep over the 106 TSX files under src, counting class tokens with their variant prefixes and opacity modifiers, and cross-checked with the script's own parser (classStrings and tokensOf), which finds the same 324 palette and hex tokens, all in code strings: none in a comment, none joined to a ${} substitution and none in a string with an escape. Raw hex counts and the gold exception: text-[#...] is 39 in 23 files and bg-[#...] 8 in 5, as the manifest says, plus 3 accent-[#1a2744] (PostsPanel.tsx 344, GradeConfirm.tsx 82, FamilyRegistrationPanel.tsx 167) and 1 hover:border-[#1877F2] (Footer.tsx 77) it does not count: 51 hex class tokens in 30 files. The exception is much larger than two strings. text-[#7a5c00] is 28 uses in 16 files (27 plus hover:text-[#7a5c00] in MemberSeatsCell.tsx 78): AuditLogPanel.tsx 40, 63, 68, 69, 71, 77; BoardSeatsPanel.tsx 126, 327; MemberSeatsCell.tsx 57, 78; MembersTable.tsx 135; TournamentList.tsx 17; TournamentWizard.tsx 373, 503; ResultsEntry.tsx 92, 107; FilterDropdown.tsx 50; MultiSelectDropdown.tsx 62; StatusBadge.tsx 35; AdminEmailPage.tsx 95, 498; BoardInboxPage.tsx 231, 232, 375; BoardPage.tsx 158; ChampionsPage.tsx 96; TournamentsPage.tsx 644; WorkspacePage.tsx 76. text-[#f0d07a] is 5 in 5 files: PageHero.tsx 75, FilterDropdown.tsx 47, MultiSelectDropdown.tsx 59, ContactPage.tsx 61, HomePage.tsx 89. Order 25 moves only StatusBadge's and PageHero's string. So 33 of the 39 hex text classes are these two golds. Decide whether every #7a5c00 and #f0d07a use waits for order 25 (allowlisted with that reason) or the other 26 #7a5c00 uses move now, and record it: text-status-soon is exactly #7a5c00 on the legacy :root (index.css line 184; #705718 under the new look at line 269 and #c8a94a in dark at line 304), while no token has #f0d07a as its legacy value (--gold-on-dark is #c8a94a, line 178). The other hex values have no token: the remaining 18 hex tokens are #9b1c1c and #1e4d7b, the urgent and info announcement tones under white text (AnnouncementBanner.tsx 16 and 17; AdminAnnouncementPanel.tsx 26 and 27, the swatches, and 286, bg-[#1e4d7b]/15 with text-[#1e4d7b]); #f2efe6, the map's ground (LCAMap.tsx 347, ClubLocationPicker.tsx 159; the same literal is in the map style in src/areas/clubs/clubMap.ts); #1877F2, the social network's brand blue (Footer.tsx 77 hover:bg and hover:border, Navbar.tsx 253 hover:text, FacebookFeed.tsx 110); #1668d8 (FacebookFeed.tsx 164 and 183); #8a6d1f (ClubDetailPage.tsx 43, a dark gold the one-off dark run under step 23 found); and accent-[#1a2744] three times. None of these values appears in src/index.css. To keep flag-off identity each needs a token whose legacy value is that literal (a fixed brand colour in the brand @theme block, like --color-brand-navy, for grounds that stay put in every look such as the two banner tones, or a semantic token with a new-look value), or it stays a raw class in the allowlist with its reason (a third-party brand colour, the map's own ground). accent-[#1a2744] has legacy-exact replacements in accent-brand-navy and accent-ink. Status classes with a legacy-exact token: of the 60 distinct palette utilities in use, 7 have a token with the same value on the legacy :root, and one of them only as the same colour written differently. text-emerald-800 (37) equals --ok and --status-open, oklch(43.2% 0.095 166.913) (index.css 174 and 182); bg-emerald-100 (25) equals --status-open-tint (183); text-red-700 (4) equals --status-full, --status-waitlist and --status-live (186, 188, 192); bg-red-100 (9) equals their tints (187, 189, 193); text-blue-800 (18) equals --status-partner (194); bg-blue-50 (3) equals --status-partner-tint (195); text-red-600 (5: AdminAnnouncementPanel.tsx 314 and 415, AdminClubPage.tsx 511, AdminEmailPage.tsx 126, BoardInboxPage.tsx 356) is --bad's colour, but --bad is written oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325) (line 175, the shadcn destructive) and red-600 oklch(57.7% 0.245 27.325) (theme.css line 16), and semantic-map.test.ts compares the resolved values to the letter (toBe), so that pair needs a numeric comparison or a recorded exception. Every other shade has no legacy-equal token: text-emerald-700 14, -600 4, -300 4, -900 2, -950 1; bg-emerald-50 12, -200 2, -500 2, -600 1, -500/20 4; border-emerald-200 11, -600 1, hover:border-emerald-600/50 1; text-red-800 6, -900 2, -300 2; bg-red-50 2 and hover:bg-red-50 3, bg-red-500/20 2; border-red-200 1; fill-red-500 1 (GovLayout.tsx 109). So 'each mapping again resolves under the legacy :root to the colour it replaces' holds only with new tokens whose legacy values are those shades (each listed in tokens.test.ts, which holds every token to today's value, lines 69 and 105 to 116, and checked in contrast.test.ts under the new look), or by keeping those classes with a reason. Also, the status tokens are built as pairs, words on their own tint: under the new look --status-live and --status-lca are #fff in base (lines 277 and 281) and --status-lca is #0b1220 in dark (316), so text-status-live or text-status-lca on a page or card would be white on white or dark on dark. Red or green text on a page or card belongs to text-bad or text-ok (or text-status-full, whose new-look values are #c0362c and #ff6b6b); only words on a status tint take a status pair. Greys and slates, which step 23 left here: text-gray-600 5 in 4 files (AdminSupportPage.tsx 25, DashboardPage.tsx 52, SupportPage.tsx 24, TournamentPrintPage.tsx 104 and 109); bg-gray-100 3, the resolved ticket badge with text-gray-600 (AdminSupportPage.tsx 25, DashboardPage.tsx 52, SupportPage.tsx 24; DashboardPage's line was 51 at step 23); border-gray-300 2 (TournamentPrintPage.tsx 101 and 171); bg-slate-400 2 (TournamentsPage.tsx 328 and 695) and bg-slate-500 1 (343), the legend dots of the state filter on /tournaments, each beside its words. No zinc, neutral or stone class is used. None equals a token on the legacy :root: text-gray-600 is oklch(44.6% 0.03 256.802) (theme.css 232) against --ink-muted oklch(0.556 0 0) (index.css 171); border-gray-300 oklch(87.2% 0.01 258.338) (229) against --hairline oklch(0.922 0 0) (172); bg-gray-100 oklch(96.7% 0.003 264.542) (227) against --surface-2 and --status-closed-tint oklch(0.97 0 0) (168, 191); bg-slate-400 oklch(70.4% 0.04 256.788) and bg-slate-500 oklch(55.4% 0.046 257.417) (218, 219) match nothing. So 'gray and slate stragglers become ink-muted or border-hairline' changes colours with newLook off, which the manifest's own rule forbids and test/a11y/baseline.json cannot see (it records body, the first Button, a table header and a font-mono element on /, /tournaments, /membership and /tournaments/fx-t-done). Give them legacy-exact tokens or keep them with a reason (the print page draws for paper and may stay fixed), and record which. Families the manifest does not name: amber 37 in 9 files (ScannerPage 9, TournamentDetailPage 9, TournamentManagePage 7, PreviewBanner 3, TournamentPrintPage 3, UsChessUploadPanel 2, UsChessMembership 2, FamilyCard 1, FamilyRegistrationPanel 1); blue 43 in 7 (AuditLogPanel 18, SupportPage 7, StatusBadge 5, AdminSupportPage 4, DashboardPage 4, TournamentsPage 3, TournamentDetailPage 2; bg-blue-100 with text-blue-800 15 times, as ticket and audit badges); green 11 in 2 (UscfSearchInput.tsx 82, 128, 328, 425, 426, 431, 439, and TournamentManagePage.tsx 1075, bg-green-500/20 text-green-300); yellow 9 in 3 (bg-yellow-100 text-yellow-800, the in-progress ticket badge, DashboardPage.tsx 51, SupportPage.tsx 23, AdminSupportPage.tsx 24, and SupportPage.tsx 354, bg-yellow-50 border-yellow-200 text-yellow-700); purple 2 (AuditLogPanel.tsx 50). The manifest names emerald, red, gray and slate; the step 21 follow-up 'Dark mode on pages not converted yet' (REDESIGN_STATUS.md line 1132) gives step 24 'the status colours, the grey and slate classes and raw hex' and keeps newLook off until both steps land; and test/a11y/dark-spot.spec.ts lines 27 to 31 already credit emerald, red, amber, green, blue, yellow, orange, gray and slate text and bg classes to this step. Decide which families this slice maps and what the ratchet watches, and record the rest with the step that owns them. Several are categories, not statuses (AuditLogPanel's action colours, the support ticket badges), which is the manifest's risk. Light tones on navy: StatusBadge's navy surface (StatusBadge.tsx 29 to 31: bg-emerald-500/20 text-emerald-300, bg-red-500/20 text-red-300, bg-blue-500/20 text-blue-200), TournamentDetailPage.tsx 38, 539 and 544, and TournamentManagePage.tsx 1075, 1084 and 1086 sit on the navy hero, which is bg-brand-navy and stays navy in every look. Like the translucent white veils step 23 kept, they may be kept with a reason. A token class with an opacity modifier falls back to its token at full strength in a browser that cannot mix colours (step 23 deviation), so any /20 tint moved to a token needs the same care as the navy tints. StatusBadge overlap: src/components/StatusBadge.tsx is order 26's file (the status prop mapped to status tokens). Its TONE_CLASSES (lines 26 to 41) hold 13 classes in this slice's families and text-[#7a5c00] (line 35, order 25), and StatusDot's open dot is bg-emerald-500 (line 80). Rewriting the light tones here is compatible with order 26 if the tone and on props keep working; record what is left to 26. Light islands (step 23 follow-up, REDESIGN_STATUS.md line 1149): the member strip on /membership is MembershipPage.tsx 183 (border-b bg-emerald-50) and the finished-event panel TournamentManagePage.tsx 2177 (border-emerald-200 bg-emerald-50); their text is text-ink since step 23. bg-emerald-50 has no legacy token (--status-open-tint is emerald-100). bg-emerald-50 also grounds the success notes in RegisterPage.tsx 141, ContactPage.tsx 76, AccountSecurityPage.tsx 196, DashboardPage.tsx 585, ForgotPasswordPage.tsx 84, TournamentDetailPage.tsx 846 and 897, SupportPage.tsx 298, FamilyRegistrationPanel.tsx 155 and PostsPanel.tsx 286, mostly with border-emerald-200 and text-emerald-800. If an island stays light in dark mode, its text-ink becomes text-brand-navy, as the follow-up says. Navy tints and navy borders, which the manifest's brief does not mention but step 23's decision 'Ink and grounds' (line 680) and its follow-ups 'Navy tints in dark mode' (line 1145) and 'Navy borders and rings' (line 1144) give to step 24. Today: the 17 faint tints are bg-brand-navy/5 5, /7 5, /8 2, /10 1, /[0.03] 1, /[0.04] 2 and /[0.06] 1; besides them /55 (the hero photo's veil), hover:/10 (the Exit button on the gold impersonation banner, ImpersonationBanner.tsx 16) and hover:/90 4 (the navy buttons) stay navy. border-lca-navy is 73 in 23 files: 33 opaque, of which 27 share their string with an opaque bg-brand-navy and 6 do not (MembersExportMenu.tsx, UscfSearchInput.tsx and AdminSupportPage.tsx beside a navy tint; ResultsEntry.tsx twice and ScannerPage.tsx once on a light ground), so the follow-up's 'the 33 opaque ones sit with a selected navy fill' holds for 27; and 40 tinted (/10 2, /15 3, /20 7, /30 1, /40 3, hover:/30 2, hover:/40 21, focus:/50 1), one of them ImpersonationBanner.tsx 16's border-lca-navy/30 on gold. ring-lca-navy is 1 (AdminAnnouncementPanel.tsx 152). Each pair resolves to #1a2744 on the legacy :root, but an ink form with a modifier falls back to full-strength navy in a browser without color-mix, which is why step 23 kept the tints; the follow-up names the fix (an @supports not (color: color-mix(in lab, red, red)) block that gives each tint in use the sRGB tint its brand class falls back to, or tint tokens whose plain :root value is that tint). Do them here with a review of each, or record why not and move the follow-ups on. semantic-map.test.ts lines 135 to 141 pin bg-brand-navy's forms ('', 5, 7, 8, 10, 55, 90, [0.03], [0.04], [0.06]) and 15 cases, so moving the tints changes those pins. The script's comment search (follow-up 'Quoted strings in comment prose', line 1154): semantic-colours.ts line 285 still takes whatever lies between two matching quote marks on one line as a quoted string. Before this slice's run, a quote mark should open or close a string only where no letter or digit stands on its outer side, with a test in test/unit/semantic-colours-edges.test.ts that puts a watched class between "don't" and "it's" in a comment and expects no rewrite. No TSX comment names a class of this slice's families today. The script's map grammar: loadMap takes watch entries, rule from and to, and keep classes only as plain utility names, /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/ (semantic-colours.ts lines 100, 113, 121 and 143), so no arbitrary hex class can be watched, ruled or kept; only a site (one string, any single token) can rewrite one. A rule matches one utility exactly, so a status map names each shade it takes. Either extend the grammar, with edge tests, or route the hex through sites and leave its watch to the ratchet. The default map is loaded by semantic-map.test.ts, semantic-map-cascade.test.ts, semantic-map-grounds.test.ts and redesign-status-step23.test.ts, and its check runs in semantic-map.test.ts (line 217) and redesign-status-step23.test.ts; the second map needs its own check in a test. The ratchet and its allowlist: a test that fails on text-lca-navy, bg-white, raw emerald or red classes or arbitrary hex classes outside an allowlist of club colours would fail on today's tree. text-lca-navy is 0 in TSX (1 in src/lib/brand.ts line 36, GOLD_BUTTON, not a TSX file), but bg-white is 39, all step 23 keep entries (5 white mats: ClubsPage, ClubDetailPage, AdminClubPage, WorkspacePage and the QR code on AccountSecurityPage; 34 translucent veils on navy), and the hex order 25 owns, and whatever this slice keeps, would be found too. Club colours are inline styles, which a class scan does not see. So the allowlist holds the kept classes with their reasons; decide whether the ratchet reads the step 23 map's keep entries rather than repeating them, and record it. The planted bg-white and text-[#123456] go in a temporary tree, as semantic-map.test.ts plants its fixtures, with the class names built at run time: Tailwind reads every file in the repository for class names (index.css sets no @source; follow-up 'Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS', line 1146), so a literal text-[#123456] in a test adds a rule to the site's CSS. The second map spells out every old class it replaces, so their rules stay in the built CSS after the pages stop using them; report the CSS size. Contrast: test/unit/contrast.test.ts already checks --ok and --bad at 4.5:1 on --ground and --surface in base, dark, live, live in dark mode, scholastic, heritage and heritage in dark mode (lines 57 to 61) and every --status-X on its own --status-X-tint (lines 67 to 69). It does not check status or ok and bad text on --surface-2 or on a tint, or any token this slice adds; extend it to every pair the map writes. The dark spot run: dark-spot.spec.ts's LATER list (lines 27 to 31) credits raw hex in text, bg and border classes and the status, grey and slate families to a later step. After this slice it should credit only what a later step still owns (text-lca-gold, text-[#7a5c00] and text-[#f0d07a] for order 25, and anything this slice records as kept), so a status or hex failure this slice leaves would fail the spec. Step 23's run found one colour-contrast failure, on /tournaments: the LCA pill, TournamentsPage.tsx 644, text-[#7a5c00] on its gold tint at 1.84:1 (#7a5c00 on #3d392b); it clears here only if this slice moves that class. Lint: 16 errors and 13 warnings at 4e4ad3a, measured with npm run lint, as at step 23. The errors are in functions/api/support.ts 1, functions/api/support/[id].ts 1, functions/utils/live/swiss/matching.ts 2, scanner/sandbox/chess-shim/src/index.ts 4, scanner/sandbox/genGames.ts 4, scanner/sandbox/perft.ts 1 and src/areas/events/components/GradeConfirm.tsx 3 (react-refresh/only-export-components at lines 18, 43 and 49: NO_TICKS, asksGrade and confirmedRange). GradeConfirm.tsx line 82 holds accent-[#1a2744], so rewriting it touches the file and its three errors must be fixed (the three exports moved to a module of their own, as step 23 did for LCAMap); list the fix. The 13 warnings sit in BoardSeatsPanel, ChampionsPanel, PostsPanel, TournamentWizard, LCAMap, FamilyCard, FamilyRegistrationPanel, UscfSearchInput, HomePage (2), ScholasticPage and TournamentsPage (2). Tokens and records: any token this slice adds goes inside the two existing @theme blocks (token-utilities.test.ts line 19 and semantic-map.test.ts require exactly two) and into tokens.test.ts with its legacy value. redesign-status-step23.test.ts pins the step 23 follow-up headings (lines 177 to 192, '- **Navy tints in dark mode (step 23).**' and nine more), the T1 row's kept counts from the step 23 map and the step 23 block, so close a step 23 follow-up by adding 'Done in step 24: ...' to it, as earlier steps do, never by renaming or removing it. No acceptance-table row owns this step: T1 covers navy text, white grounds and navy bands, so widen T1 or add a row in the table's own pattern. Brief: REDESIGN_SPEC.md WS01 names no status codemod and no raw-colour ratchet; its only status rule is that StatusBadge's tones map to status tokens (line 303), which is order 26. This step comes from the plan, because dark follows the device as soon as newLook is on with no separate darkMode flag (decision 6 in the lead's notes). Build size: npm run check:bundle checks only that no zod reaches dist/assets and measures no size; step 23 recorded CSS 113,933 bytes and JavaScript 2,568,712 bytes in 104 files, 127 files in all, so report the built CSS and JS sizes before and after. Environment detail: package.json still carries 38 caret ranges from before the redesign; the exact-pin rule applies to any package this slice adds.

Gate before reporting: npm run lint (baseline 16 errors and 13 warnings, measured on this tree; the error total never rises from 16 and every error in a touched file is fixed; report before and after), npm run build, npm run typecheck:functions, npm run check:bundle, npm run test:all (unit 2426 in 103 files and integration 790 in 58 files before this slice; report the counts), and then PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y end to end in this container with its output quoted (both builds, the flag-off baseline compared and unchanged, the dark spot run's results; 122 passed and 27 skipped before this slice). test/a11y/baseline.json must not be rewritten: with newLook off nothing visible changes, and a baseline difference is a defect in the slice. If an integration file fails to load as a whole on the first run, rerun that file alone once before treating it as real. Standing rules: no AI references anywhere, in code, code comments, docs or commit text; read the real file before changing it; match repo conventions; WCAG 2.2 AA; plain language ('US Chess', a weekday on every date, '7:00 PM'); no em dashes in anything you write; fixtures contain nothing real; new packages exact-pinned. The recorder updates REDESIGN_STATUS.md (a step 24 block; the acceptance table row this slice proves, added in the table's own pattern if none fits; decisions; deviations; the judgement calls; each resolved verify item; the counts) and, if the slice deviates from the brief, the step 24 sentence in the WS01 deviations list of docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md, and drafts the commit text into <scratchpad>/slice24-commit.txt: a subject under 72 characters and plain prose, no attribution or co-author lines, no session links, no em dashes. The step records, the acceptance table and Decisions must not use the words slice, builder, scout, planner, recorder, manifest, subagent, workflow or the phrase the lead.
files: scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.ts (the comment quote fix, and the map grammar only if it is extended for hex classes)
test/unit/contrast.test.ts (the status text pairs the map writes)
test/a11y/dark-spot.spec.ts (the LATER list narrowed to what a later step still owns)
docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (the step 24 deviation sentence, only if needed)
acceptance: Gate green, test/a11y/baseline.json unchanged, and the build size change reported (dist/assets CSS and JS sizes before and after)
raw-colours.test.ts passes on the codebase and fails on a planted bg-white or text-[#123456] outside the allowlist (planted in a temporary tree, with the class names built at run time)
Flag-off colours unchanged: semantic-map.test.ts extended so every pair the status map writes resolves on the legacy :root to the colour it replaces, and the a11y-off baseline unchanged
With newLook on, status text in dark and live reaches 4.5:1 (contrast.test.ts extended to every pair the map writes)
REDESIGN_STATUS.md records this slice's acceptance row, the judgement calls, any deviation and each resolved verify item
